alternatives.note: R1 pipeline; correct global step but missing the blur step. Pair0 reaches 43.97 dB only because 66.9% of its pixels are clipped to 0, which masks a mild sigma=1 gaussian blur.
Control only (pair0): non-commuting reversed order, finite 52.10 dB and CI unique diffs -7/-3/-3; rejects this order and proves the inf result of blur->gamma is not a copy artifact.

analysis.mode: PSNR (noise_prior sigma 0.62/1.48/0.74 << noise_gaussian sev1 = 12.75 grey levels -> no random noise)
analysis.rationale: R2 adds the missing optical blur on top of R1's confirmed global tone map: blur_gaussian:1 followed by brightness_darken_gamma_HSV:5 reproduces all three support pairs pixel-exactly (PSNR = inf dB, CI 10/10, every CI metric diff 0.000 on pairs 0/1/2). Signals that motivated the hypothesis: pair2 full_analysis independently flags blur (gm_ratio 0.6627 < 0.85, spectral_slope_ratio 1.0914 > 1.08, residual_anisotropy 1.375 < 1.7 so not motion, glass_score 0.2998); pair0/pair1 show weaker blur evidence (gm_ratio 0.2506/0.3453, slope ratios 0.928/1.010) because heavy clipping (66.9%/26.4% pixels <= 1) masks a mild sigma=1 blur, and R1's peeled residual after gamma-only was structured and slightly smoother than the simulation (hf_lf diff 25%, zero_crossing 39%). The exact match also shows pair2's glass flag was a false positive of glass_score and the true blur subtype is gaussian severity 1. Order is identified, not assumed: reversed order (gamma then blur) is non-commuting and only reaches 52.10 dB on pair0 (CI 9/10, unique diffs -7/-3/-3), versus pixel-exact for blur->gamma on 3/3 pairs. Note pair0's gamma-only 43.97 dB (>40 dB) was an over-confident LIKELY for an incomplete pipeline; only k=3 exact support matching exposes the missing step. This pipeline corresponds to the sampler's physical order blur(priority 1) -> brightness(priority 2).

analysis.coupling_notes: Blur is applied before the global tone map (sampler physical order: blur priority 1, brightness priority 2). Because the tone map compresses V with gamma 3.5, most of the blur signature is destroyed except in the least-clipped pair (pair2, 13.7% zeros), which is exactly where run_full_analysis detects it; pair0's 66.9% clipping makes even a wrong (blur-less) pipeline score >40 dB. The R1 residual-intensity correlation (ivc 0.9974) came from residual structure of the missing blur interacting with the tone curve, not from a gamma-severity error.
analysis.k_limitation: k=3 support pairs only; no external data added. Pair0 is the primary alias (degraded.png). All three pairs were used for validation.
